requirements.verifier_assertion: test.sh:50 requires /app/ars.R to exist as a regular file.
test.sh:51 requires /app/results.tsv to exist as a regular file.
Instruction: `Rscript /app/ars.R` performs the batch run; the RVER heredoc verifies results.tsv is produced by that run.
test.sh:77-79 sources ars.R from a scratch directory and asserts (a) sourcing returned success, (b) no new files landed in that directory as a side effect.
must_include: loadable with `source("/app/ars.R")` without any side effects
no sampling, printing, or file writes at source time

requirements.verifier_assertion: test.sh:82-97 negative-path RNEG block calls `ars(...)` after sourcing; ars.R must export a function named `ars`. Instruction also mandates a `test()` export.

requirements.verifier_assertion: test.sh:52 and RVER file.path(app, "inputs/data/cases.tsv") anchor the cases fixture at /app/inputs/data/cases.tsv with tab separator and header row.
test.sh:53 and RVER file.path(app, "inputs/data/overrides.tsv") anchor the overrides fixture at /app/inputs/data/overrides.tsv.

RVER accesses cs$case_id / cs$family / cs$params / cs$support / cs$n / cs$mean_tol / cs$sd_tol and reads cases.tsv with colClasses=character and strip.white=FALSE — those columns must exist in that order.

RVER dens() switch dispatches on family ∈ {gamma, weibull, exp, normal, logistic, beta} with specific density formulas per family; the sampled values are checked against those exact target densities via numerical integration of the moments.
RVER pparse() splits `params` on `;` and each entry on `=`. `params` must be a `;`-separated list of `key=value` pairs.
RVER strsplit(sup, ",", fixed=TRUE) then as.numeric — support is `lo,hi`. Test.sh:82-97 also passes c(0, Inf) to ars(), so ±Inf endpoints must be accepted.
RVER coerces n via as.integer and compares abs(sm-tm$mean) > mt / abs(ss-tm$sd) > st for tolerances; instruction requires positive integer n and positive-real tolerances.
Instruction says empty initial_points is valid; cases.tsv rows like `gamma_a` and `exp_a` have empty initial_points and are still expected to PASS.
must_include: empty (empty means the sampler chooses its own starting abscissae)

requirements.verifier_assertion: RVER applies overrides only when the trimmed column value is non-empty, and matches on exact ov$case_id[i] == cs$case_id[j]. Instruction: override wins on match; matching is exact string.
must_include: override values replace the ones in cases.tsv

requirements.verifier_assertion: RVER `cs <- cs[!duplicated(cs$case_id, fromLast=TRUE), , drop=FALSE]` — keep last exact-id occurrence. Test.sh:200-201 asserts n_samples for dupc == 4000 (the last of two `dupc` rows).
must_include: de-duplicate by keeping the LAST occurrence

requirements.verifier_assertion: RVER lines 160-161 assert both `dupc` and ` dupc` (with leading space) appear in results — near-duplicate case_ids differing by whitespace are distinct rows and must all be processed.
must_include: differ only by surrounding whitespace or by letter case are DISTINCT

requirements.verifier_assertion: RVER `invalid <- miss(fam)||miss(par)||miss(sup)||miss(nn)` → status must be ERROR with n_samples=0 and sample_mean/sd = NA and no sample file present. Test.sh:202-203 anchors bad_missing → ERROR (empty family).
test.sh:82-97 requires ars() to raise R errors for: n=-3 (non-positive), n=3.5 (non-integer), support c(5,1) (reversed), support c(NA,1) (non-finite), logf=42 (non-function callback).
test.sh:94-95 asserts `s <- ars(lf, 40, c(0, Inf))` returns 40 finite values all strictly > 0 for the gamma(shape=2, rate=1) log density.
must_include: one finite numeric value per line
every value inside the `support` interval `[lo, hi]`

requirements.verifier_assertion: test.sh:92-93 asserts ars() errors on `bimodal <- function(x) log(exp(-(x-2)^2/0.2)+exp(-(x+2)^2/0.2))`. RVER logconcave() classifies beta a=0.5 b=0.5 as non-log-concave, so ncv must land as status ERROR. Test.sh:204-205 anchors ncv → ERROR.
must_include: raise an R error for a target that is not log-concave
the other cases are still processed

requirements.verifier_assertion: RVER `if (!identical(names(res), c("case_id","status","n_samples","sample_mean","sample_sd"))) stop2` — header must be exactly these five column names in this order, tab-separated (read.delim with sep="\t").
RVER `if (!identical(res$case_id, res$case_id[order(res$case_id, method="radix")])) stop2` — rows sorted by case_id via method="radix" (byte-order, NOT locale).
must_include: sorted by `case_id` in ASCENDING BYTE order

requirements.verifier_assertion: RVER `if (nrow(res) != nrow(cs)) stop2` — results.tsv row count must equal the resolved cases count (post-dedup, per instruction).

RVER asserts r$status ∈ {PASS, FAIL, ERROR} implicitly (specific comparisons for each). ERROR fields checked: n_samples==0, upper(sample_mean)=="NA", upper(sample_sd)=="NA", no sample file. Valid case: status=="PASS", n_samples==nval, sample file finite in support, mean/sd within tol.
must_include: sample mean AND sample sd are both within `mean_tol` / `sd_tol`
target's TRUE mean and sd on the support
FAIL = valid case out of tolerance
ERROR = invalid row or non-log-concave target

requirements.verifier_assertion: RVER reads case_<cid>_samples.txt with readLines + as.numeric and asserts length==nval, all is.finite, and all in [support[1], support[2]]; for invalid rows RVER asserts the sample file does NOT exist.
must_include: one finite numeric value per line
every value inside the `support` interval `[lo, hi]`

requirements.verifier_assertion: Instruction: `set.seed(20260812)` before the batch run so results are reproducible. Test.sh runs the same seed-driven Rscript twice (solution then RVER retrieves the outputs) and expects them to be consistent.

Instruction: numeric fields printed with 6 digits after the decimal; n_samples is an integer. RVER's `as.integer(r$n_samples)` and `as.numeric(r$sample_mean)` succeed only if these formats are respected.

RVER computes numerical-integration ground-truth mean/sd and tolerance-checks sample mean/sd — hard-coded / constant outputs will not pass because the sample must be a real draw from the target for arbitrary families. Instruction: sampling must be genuine, not precomputed constants.
must_include: draw random values from every specified family via rejection sampling
